sources: RICS Home Survey Standard, UK, 1st Edition (2021)
BRE Digest 251: Assessment of damage in low-rise buildings (1995)
CUBIT-Det – Zhao et al., Automation in Construction 2024

rics_condition_ratings.1: No repair currently needed. Maintain in normal way.
rics_condition_ratings.2: Defects needing repair or replacement, not serious or urgent.
rics_condition_ratings.3: Serious defects needing urgent repair, replacement, or investigation.
rics_condition_ratings.R: Documents to request before contract exchange.

defect_categories.description: Defects arising from foundation movement, structural loading, or building element failure

defect_types.description: Diagonal or stepped cracking caused by downward foundation movement, typically tapered with wider end indicating direction of drop
possible_causes: Clay soil shrinkage from tree root water extraction
Defective drains leaking into subsoil and washing away fines
Mining activity or dissolution of soluble substrata
defect_types.recommended_action: Urgent structural engineer investigation; CCTV drain survey; arboricultural assessment if trees nearby; crack monitoring (BRE method); possible underpinning; notify insurer

defect_types.description: Cracking from normal consolidation of ground under building weight, typically stable and historic
possible_causes: Normal ground consolidation in first few years after construction
Variations in foundation depth or bearing strata
defect_types.recommended_action: Monitor for progression; if stable, cosmetic repair only; fill and redecorate

defect_types.description: Upward ground movement causing cracking and distortion, often after tree removal on clay soils
possible_causes: Removal of mature trees causing clay re-expansion
defect_types.recommended_action: Structural engineer assessment; tree management plan; drainage investigation; possible foundation strengthening

defect_types.description: Horizontal cracking along bed joints caused by corroding cavity wall ties expanding within mortar, potentially leading to outer leaf instability
possible_causes: Corrosion of mild steel ties (especially pre-1981 properties)
Coastal or industrial pollution accelerating corrosion
defect_types.recommended_action: Specialist wall tie survey with borescope; install new stainless steel remedial ties; isolate corroded ties; repoint affected areas; structural crack stitching if needed

defect_types.description: Cracking above window or door openings from corroded, rotted, or inadequate lintels
possible_causes: Corrosion of steel lintel causing expansion
defect_types.recommended_action: Temporary support with Acrow props; replace lintel; rebuild masonry above; check all other lintels of same type

defect_types.description: Outward thrust of walls at eaves level caused by inadequately restrained roof structure
possible_causes: Inadequate collar ties or lateral restraint
Re-roofing with heavier coverings without structural upgrade
Removal of structural members during loft conversion
defect_types.recommended_action: Structural engineer assessment; install collar ties and lateral restraint straps; may require partial roof rebuild

defect_types.description: Failed or deteriorated floor joists causing bouncy, springy, or uneven floors
possible_causes: Wet or dry rot at joist ends bearing in external walls
Excessive notching or drilling for services
defect_types.recommended_action: Specialist timber survey; replace or sister affected joists; improve sub-floor ventilation; treat rot; address moisture source

defect_types.description: Structural distress from unauthorised removal of load-bearing walls without adequate support
defect_types.recommended_action: Structural engineer assessment; install appropriate steel beam with Building Regulations approval; retrospective regularisation application

defect_categories.description: Cracks that are cosmetic or related to thermal/moisture movement rather than structural failure

defect_types.description: Very fine cracks under 0.1mm typically from normal thermal or moisture movement
possible_causes: Plaster or render shrinkage during drying
defect_types.recommended_action: No action required; cosmetic redecoration during normal maintenance

defect_types.description: Fine cracks up to 5mm, typically aesthetic requiring only filling and redecoration
possible_causes: Differential movement between masonry and studwork
defect_types.recommended_action: Fill and redecorate; external repointing if in mortar joints; monitor for progression

defect_types.description: Cracking within external render coat, may indicate underlying movement or material incompatibility
possible_causes: Hard cement render on soft substrate (common in older properties)
defect_types.recommended_action: Hack off cracked areas and patch repair; consider lime render for pre-1920s buildings; investigate if cracking pattern suggests structural cause

defect_types.description: Cracking to ceiling surfaces, often at ceiling-to-wall junctions or in lath-and-plaster ceilings
possible_causes: Differential thermal movement at junction of dissimilar materials
Vibration from traffic or building use
defect_types.recommended_action: Cosmetic: fill and redecorate. If lath-and-plaster showing detachment or sagging, consider overboarding or replacement

defect_categories.description: All forms of unwanted moisture ingress or retention within the building fabric

defect_types.description: Moisture rising from the ground through masonry by capillary action due to failed or absent damp-proof course
possible_causes: Bridged DPC from raised external ground levels
Failed damp-proof membrane (DPM) in solid floors
defect_types.recommended_action: Identify cause; reduce external ground levels to minimum 150mm below DPC; repair or install DPC; strip non-breathable plaster and re-plaster with lime-based breathable plaster; install DPM to floors if needed

defect_types.description: Moisture entering through the external building envelope due to defects in weatherproofing
possible_causes: Missing or blocked gutters and downpipes
Failed window or door drip details
defect_types.recommended_action: Repair all defects to external envelope; repoint with appropriate mortar; repair rainwater goods; reinstate drip details; allow to dry out before redecorating

defect_types.description: Moisture forming on cold surfaces when warm moist air reaches dew point, the most common form of dampness in UK dwellings
possible_causes: Poor thermal insulation creating cold surfaces
High moisture production from cooking, bathing, drying clothes
defect_types.recommended_action: Improve ventilation (extract fans in kitchens and bathrooms, trickle vents to windows); improve insulation; maintain background heating; consider positive input ventilation (PIV) unit

defect_types.description: Condensation forming within the building fabric structure, often undetected until damage is advanced
possible_causes: Warm moist air penetrating construction and condensing within walls or roof
Incorrect vapour barrier placement after retrofit insulation
Inadequate ventilation to roof space or cavity
defect_types.recommended_action: Specialist assessment; improve ventilation; install or relocate vapour control layer; review insulation specification; check for consequential timber decay

defect_types.description: Dampness caused by leaking pipes, overflows, or defective waste connections (traumatic dampness)
possible_causes: Defective overflow from tanks or cisterns
defect_types.recommended_action: Locate and repair leak urgently; assess extent of water damage; check for consequential timber rot; dry out affected areas

defect_types.description: Damp-proof course rendered ineffective by external material creating a moisture bridge above the DPC line
possible_causes: External ground or paving raised above DPC level
Earth or soil banked against walls
External render taken below DPC line
defect_types.recommended_action: Reduce external ground levels to minimum 150mm below DPC; hack back render below DPC; install channel drain at wall base if ground cannot be lowered

defect_categories.description: Defects to roof coverings, structure, flashings, and associated elements

defect_types.description: Roof tiles or slates displaced or absent, exposing underlay or roof structure to weather
possible_causes: Nail fatigue (nail sickness) due to corrosion
Wind damage lifting or dislodging tiles
Frost damage causing delamination of slates
Failed mortar bedding (verge or valley tiles)
defect_types.recommended_action: Replace individual tiles or slates; if widespread nail fatigue, full re-roofing likely needed; check for consequential water ingress damage

defect_types.description: Loose, displaced, or missing ridge tiles along roof apex
defect_types.recommended_action: Re-bed ridge tiles with appropriate mortar or install mechanical dry ridge system; check for water ingress

defect_types.description: Defects to flat roof covering including blistering, ponding, and membrane deterioration
possible_causes: End of service life (felt roofs typically 10-15 years)
Inadequate falls causing ponding (should be minimum 1:80)
defect_types.recommended_action: Patch repair if localised; full replacement with modern single-ply membrane (EPDM or GRP) if widespread; improve falls and drainage; typical flat roof lifespan is shorter than pitched

defect_types.description: Failed or defective flashings at junctions between roof and walls, chimneys, or other penetrations
possible_causes: Thermal creep and fatigue cracking of lead
Mortar fillet used instead of proper lead flashing
Corrosion of zinc or other metal flashings
defect_types.recommended_action: Renew or re-dress lead flashings; replace mortar fillets with proper lead work (code 4 or 5 lead); chase into masonry and point

defect_types.description: Defects to chimney stack including leaning, deteriorated masonry, failed flaunching, and loose pots
possible_causes: Sulphate attack from flue gases deteriorating morite mortar
Differential drying causing lean toward prevailing weather
Removed chimney breast below without adequate support
defect_types.recommended_action: Monitor lean; repoint deteriorated masonry; re-flaunch chimney pots; cap unused flues with ventilated cowls; install flue liner; partial rebuild in severe cases

defect_types.description: Defective, blocked, or missing gutters and downpipes causing water overflow and wall saturation
possible_causes: Corroded or cracked cast iron gutters
Inadequate gutter size for roof area
defect_types.recommended_action: Clear all blockages; repair or replace defective sections; ensure correct falls to outlets; consider gutter guard to prevent leaf accumulation

defect_types.description: Visible deflection or sagging of ridge line, rafters, or purlins indicating structural distress
possible_causes: Re-roofing with heavier coverings without structural upgrade
Removal of structural members for loft conversion
defect_types.recommended_action: Structural engineer assessment; sistering or replacement of affected timbers; Building Regulations regularisation if unauthorised alterations found

defect_categories.description: Deterioration of building material surfaces including spalling, peeling, efflorescence, and erosion

defect_types.description: Face of bricks or stone breaking away due to frost action, leaving exposed aggregate or crumbling surfaces
possible_causes: Hard cement pointing trapping moisture in soft bricks
Sulphate attack on mortar and bricks
Use of non-frost-resistant bricks in exposed locations
defect_types.recommended_action: Replace individual affected bricks; repoint with lime mortar to allow moisture escape; improve rainwater disposal to reduce wall saturation

defect_types.description: Concrete surface breaking away, potentially exposing reinforcement to further corrosion
possible_causes: Carbonation of concrete reducing alkalinity protecting reinforcement
Chloride ingress causing reinforcement corrosion and expansion
defect_types.recommended_action: Assess extent of carbonation and reinforcement corrosion; patch repair with compatible cementitious material; apply protective coating; structural assessment if reinforcement significantly compromised

defect_types.description: Paint or coating detaching from substrate surface
possible_causes: Incompatible paint system (e.g., non-breathable paint on lime render)
defect_types.recommended_action: Remove loose paint; prepare surface; apply appropriate breathable paint system on older buildings; address underlying moisture if present

defect_types.description: White crystalline salt deposits on masonry surfaces caused by moisture dissolving salts within the construction and depositing them on evaporation
possible_causes: New construction drying out (typically harmless and temporary)
Use of unsuitable aggregates or bricks with high salt content
defect_types.recommended_action: Brush off dry deposits; if persistent, investigate and address moisture source; avoid washing with water as this can re-dissolve and redistribute salts

defect_types.description: Weathered or deteriorated mortar joints in brickwork or stonework reducing weather resistance
possible_causes: Use of weak lime mortar in exposed locations (historic buildings)
defect_types.recommended_action: Rake out defective mortar to minimum 15mm depth and repoint; use lime mortar on pre-1920s properties to maintain breathability; match mortar profile to original

defect_types.description: External render separating from substrate, sounding hollow when tapped (blown render)
possible_causes: Moisture trapped behind impermeable cement render
Loss of adhesion from age or movement
Incompatible render specification on historic substrates
defect_types.recommended_action: Hack off all blown render to sound substrate; re-render with appropriate specification (lime render for pre-1920s); consider mesh reinforcement

defect_types.description: Discolouration of building surfaces from moisture, iron run-off, pollution, or organic matter
possible_causes: Water run-off from corroded metals (iron, copper)
Water ingress staining internal ceilings and walls
defect_types.recommended_action: Clean surfaces with appropriate method; identify and address moisture or contamination source; apply stain block before redecorating internally

defect_types.description: Visible rusting of steel reinforcement or embedded metals, often with associated concrete spalling
defect_types.recommended_action: Structural engineer assessment; break out loose concrete; clean and treat exposed reinforcement; patch with proprietary repair mortar; apply protective coating

defect_categories.description: Biological growth on surfaces and biological decay of building materials including timber rot and insect attack

defect_types.description: Biological growth on external building surfaces indicating persistent dampness
possible_causes: Persistent dampness on north-facing or shaded elevations
defect_types.recommended_action: Clean surfaces with appropriate biocide; address underlying dampness; improve drainage and ventilation to affected areas

defect_types.description: Ivy or other climbing plants with roots penetrating mortar joints and causing physical damage to masonry
possible_causes: Unchecked plant growth over extended period
Root systems penetrating and expanding within mortar joints
Retention of moisture against wall surface
defect_types.recommended_action: Careful removal (do not pull stems from wall face as this damages masonry); cut at base and allow to die before removal; repair mortar joints; ongoing monitoring

defect_types.description: Visible mould on internal surfaces, primarily a health hazard linked to dampness and poor ventilation
possible_causes: Cold bridging creating localised cold spots
defect_types.recommended_action: Treat with appropriate fungicidal wash; identify and address moisture source; improve ventilation and heating; improve insulation to eliminate cold surfaces

defect_types.description: Serious fungal decay (Serpula lacrymans) that can spread through masonry and destroy timber, requiring urgent specialist treatment
possible_causes: Prolonged damp conditions with timber moisture content above 20%
Poor ventilation to sub-floor spaces or roof voids
Blocked air bricks or sub-floor vents
defect_types.recommended_action: Urgent specialist dry rot survey; eliminate moisture source; cut back affected timber minimum 1 metre beyond visible decay; treat surrounding masonry with fungicide; improve ventilation; replace with pre-treated timber

defect_types.description: Fungal decay of timber maintained in persistently damp conditions, typically localised to the area of moisture
possible_causes: Direct water contact from leaks or defective detailing
Failed paint coatings allowing moisture absorption
Timber in contact with damp masonry
Poor maintenance of window and door joinery
defect_types.recommended_action: Identify and eliminate moisture source; cut out and replace affected timber; splice or repair where possible; improve decoration and maintenance regime

defect_types.description: Wood-boring insect attack, most commonly Common Furniture Beetle (Anobium punctatum) in UK properties
possible_causes: Damp conditions in poorly ventilated spaces
Historical infestation (very common in pre-1960s UK properties)
defect_types.recommended_action: Determine if active (fresh frass around flight holes indicates activity); if active, specialist timber treatment; improve ventilation; replace severely weakened timbers; inactive historic infestation often requires no treatment

defect_categories.description: Defects specific to window and door elements including glazing, frames, and associated components

defect_types.description: Failed double glazing with moisture between panes causing misting or condensation within the sealed unit
possible_causes: Perimeter seal failure due to age (typical life 15-25 years)
Water ingress to frame causing seal deterioration
defect_types.recommended_action: Replace failed sealed units (glass-only replacement possible, full frame replacement not always necessary)

defect_types.description: Deterioration of window or door frames from rot, corrosion, or material degradation
possible_causes: Lack of maintenance allowing moisture ingress
defect_types.recommended_action: Repair or replace frames; upgrade to current thermal standards where possible; consider planning restrictions on listed buildings or conservation areas

defect_types.description: Deteriorated, cracked, or poorly detailed window sill allowing water to track back to wall face
possible_causes: Mortar fillet replacing proper sill detail
defect_types.recommended_action: Repair or replace sill; reinstate drip detail; ensure adequate projection and weathering

defect_categories.description: Defects to building services including electrical, gas, plumbing, heating, and drainage installations

defect_types.description: Electrical installation showing signs of age, non-compliance, or potential danger
possible_causes: Plastic consumer unit without RCD protection
defect_types.recommended_action: Commission Electrical Installation Condition Report (EICR) from qualified electrician; budget for partial or full rewire and consumer unit upgrade; serious fire risk in older installations

defect_types.description: Gas installation showing signs of non-compliance or potential danger
defect_types.recommended_action: Request Gas Safety Certificate from seller; Gas Safe engineer inspection before use; install CO detectors; do NOT use appliances until confirmed safe

defect_types.description: Heating system approaching end of service life or operating inefficiently
defect_types.recommended_action: Gas Safe engineer assessment; annual service; consider replacement if over 15 years; upgrade controls for efficiency

defect_types.description: Below-ground drainage showing signs of failure, blockage, or collapse
possible_causes: Tree root ingress into pipe joints
defect_types.recommended_action: CCTV drain survey to establish extent; repair, reline, or replace defective sections; clear blockages; re-grade where needed

defect_types.description: Lead water supply pipes posing a health risk, commonly found in pre-1970s UK properties
possible_causes: Original pre-1970s lead supply pipe still in use
defect_types.recommended_action: Replace all lead supply pipework with copper or plastic; water company may replace mains-to-boundary section free of charge

defect_categories.description: Presence of materials posing health or safety risks to occupants

defect_types.description: Materials containing asbestos fibres, commonly found in pre-2000 UK buildings in various locations
possible_causes: Original construction materials (very common in 1950s-1980s buildings)
Present in artex textured coatings, floor tiles, insulating boards, pipe lagging, roof sheets, flue pipes, soffits
defect_types.recommended_action: Do not disturb; commission asbestos survey (R&D type or Management type) before any works; if in good condition and undisturbed, manage in place with labelling; if damaged or before renovation, licensed removal contractor required

defect_types.description: Naturally occurring radioactive gas seeping from ground into buildings, concentrated in certain geological areas
defect_types.recommended_action: Check radon risk map (UKradon.org); commission radon test if in affected area; install radon sump or positive ventilation if above action level (200 Bq/m³)
